newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea Kim's son to be summoned again on scandal.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea Kim's son to be summoned again on scandal.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors will again summon President Kim Young-Sam's son for questioning in connection with a probe into a scandal involving the younger Kim, a prosecution official said on Wednesday.
The official confirmed a report by state-run Korean Broadcasting System (KBS) television that Kim Hyun-chul would be summoned by 2 p.m. (0500 GMT) on Thursday.
He declined to give any more information.

KBS reported prosecutors had discovered Kim Hyun-chul, the president's second son, had managed more than 20 billion won ($22.4 million) in illicit funds, part of which came from several companies run by his associates.
Kim Hyun-chul has denied allegations he took kickbacks from companies in return for influence-peddling and that he meddled in state affairs.
He was questioned by prosecutors in February but cleared of any wrongdoing in connection with a loans-for-kickbacks scandal uncovered by the collapse in January of Hanbo Steel Co.
Hanbo, the nation's second-largest steelmaker, folded after piling up five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans, revealing a web of corrupt alliances between politicians, businessmen and bankers.
Eleven people, including ruling and opposition party lawmakers, top aides to President Kim, bankers and Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo, are on trial for bribery.
Prosecutors have said they could not find any link between Kim Hyun-chul and Hanbo but secured enough evidence to charge him this month for "irregularities unrelated to Hanbo".

Kim Hyun-chul's two business associates -- Park Tae-joong and Kim Hi-chang -- have been arrested on charges of taking bribes in return for promises to lobby the younger Kim to help obtain government broadcast licences.
Last week, the Chosun Ilbo newspaper reported Kim Ki-sup, a former top intelligence officer, had asked the Hansol Group to manage a fund worth seven billion won. Hansol has denied the report.
Kim Hyun-chul, who helped engineer his father's win in the 1992 presidential election, is also under investigation over allegations that he had kept part of the unspent funds.
Financing of the 1992 vote and the Hanbo scandal have emerged as the most explosive political issues in the run-up to the presidential elections in December.
President Kim's five-year single term expires next February and he is barred by the constitution from seeking re-election.

The main opposition National Congress for New Politics party has alleged Kim Hyun-chul pressured banks to keep loans rolling into Hanbo Steel in return for a donation worth tens of billions of won to help finance the 1992 campaign. Kim has denied this. ($1 = 893 won)
